messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Multiple GPU driver resets and OOMs observed on node gpu-25 (region-us-west2). Auto-remediation triggered: cordon/drain candidate. Priority: P1.

oncall-jordan: I'm live, joining. seeing steady Xid 79 + container OOMs. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/incidents/2735012345 :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sre_lead: quick snapshot — is this a hardware ECC pattern or driver memory leak? any kernel oops in dmesg?

eng-runtime: dmesg snippet from gpu-25 a few minutes ago:```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=1234, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679002] nvidia: GPU reported a non-recoverable error, resetting the GPU.
[ 12345.680100] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 23456 (python) total-vm:10240000kB
```

ops_anita: kube events show repeated OOMKilled for the inference containers on that node:```
$ kubectl get events -n infra | grep gpu-25
19m        Warning   OOMKilled       pod/inference-abcde       Container crashed due to OOM
```

alex: Looks like a mix: driver resets (Xid 79) coincide with container OOMs. early theory: one noisy pod triggers large GPU mem allocation pattern, driver hits unrecoverable state, kernel OOMs follow.

maria: Which customers are on that node? I'm pulling allocation map.

customer-bridge-bot: Customer impact: 2 dedicated deployments (cust-omega, cust-kite) experienced transient failed requests between 2025-03-12T14:08 and 14:17 UTC. Retries succeeded. No elevated error for hosted tier.

cs-sam: I pinged cust-omega — they saw a short spike of 5xx on their real-time scoring endpoint. No data loss, just increased latency + a handful of failed tokens. We'll prepare a short customer note.

sre_lead: Triage plan: 1) cordon gpu-25 2) drain non-daemon pods with --force/--delete-local-data if needed 3) migrate affected customers to fallback routing group 4) collect nvdiag logs and kdump 5) if repeats, place node in quarantine.

oncall-jordan: cordoning now.```
kubectl cordon gpu-25
node/gpu-25 cordoned
kubectl drain gpu-25 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
```

eng-runtime: While draining, I enabled fallback routing for cust-omega/cust-kite to route to dedicated-burst pool. Applied annotations:```
kubectl annotate ns cust-omega redwood/fallback-capable=true --overwrite
```

ops_anita: drain in progress, a couple of pods stuck Terminating due to preStop hooks. Force-deleting those to speed up.

incident-bot: ACTION: nv-host-reset monitor tripped 3x in 10m on gpu-25. Escalating to hardware queue.

alex: grabbing full nvml logs for root cause. running:```
/usr/local/bin/nvdiag --collect-all --output /tmp/nvdiag-gpu-25.tgz && gsutil cp /tmp/nvdiag-gpu-25.tgz gs://redwood-infra-diagnostics/2735012345/
```

maria: Also enabling driver debug logging on the node for next 15m:```
sudo nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,DIAG,PCIE
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-dcgm
```

eng-runtime: Observed pattern in telemetry: peak vram allocations at 14:07:40, then sustained fragmentation and repeated allocations starting at 14:08:02, driver reset 14:08:05, host OOMs 14:08:06-14:09:00. Suggests per-process allocation spike.

cs-sam: Customer comms: drafting note to cust-omega: short-lived 5xxs during 14:08-14:17 UTC; retries succeeded; we applied routing fallback and will follow up with post-incident summary.

ops_anita: Node drained successfully. setting node label quarantine=true and taking out of service.```
kubectl label node gpu-25 redwood/quarantine=true --overwrite
```

incident-bot: NOTE: hardware-case-creation triggered (case #HW-99821) and oncall notified hardware squad.

oncall-jordan: Handoff to hardware and runtime teams for deep-dive. I've attached nvdiag bundle and kernel logs to the case. Leaving oncall, handing to eng-runtime for followthrough.

eng-runtime: Will own RCA. Initial suspicion: memory hotplug fragmentation + a large unbounded allocation from an inference job. We'll search for any jobs that bypass our enforced soft-limits.

alex: Found a pod with pinned GPU memory > 98% prior to reset: pod/inference-experiments-xyz. The job ran a memory-heavy beam search. Policy breach: GPU_REQUEST=0 not set. I'm escalating to runtime policy enforcement.

maria: Quick mitigation: add pod admission webhook rule to block PODs without GPU_REQUEST or override to capped allocation for now. rolling out patch to admission controller.

incident-bot: REMINDER: Create a postmortem ticket and include following artifacts: nvdiag bundle, kdump, pod spec for inference-experiments-xyz, telemetry spike graphs.

cs-sam: I'll send the interim customer note. Suggest we offer a timeline for full report within 48 hours.

sre_lead: Good. For follow-up: 1) enforce GPU allocation caps 2) patch admission controller 3) hardware techs to run GPU memory stress test on gpu-25 in lab 4) check for similar allocation patterns across fleet and quarantine any nodes with >3 resets in 24h.

eng-runtime: I'll run a fleet scan query tomorrow: find pods with GPU_REQUEST unset and memory high-water marks.

oncall-jordan: signing off — leave any action items here. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

alex: action: open runtime ticket RT-4732 to add enforcement + add alert for 'gpu-alloc > 90% for >2m'

maria: action: follow up with hardware once bench results available.

customer-bridge-bot: Bridge closed. No active customer bridge required; customers notified.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: node gpu-25 quarantined; impacted customers routed to fallback; hardware case opened. Please continue updates in this thread for RCA notes and postmortem draft.
